title: How Much Does a Professional Website Cost? 2026 Pricing Guide
excerpt: Website quotes range from €800 to €50,000+. Here's what actually drives the difference — and what you should expect for each type of project.

blocks.text: Three agencies. Three wildly different quotes. This happens every day, and it's not dishonesty — it's that 'website' means something fundamentally different depending on who you ask.
This guide breaks down what a professional website actually costs in 2026, what drives prices up, and what you should expect to get for each budget level.
Why Website Prices Vary So Dramatically
Two websites can look nearly identical and differ by €10,000. The gap is almost never about design — it's about what's underneath.

items: Strategic copy and UX vs. filler text
Long-term support included vs. billed per hour

blocks.text: The cheapest quote often reflects the cheapest approach. The most expensive quote doesn't always mean the best result. Here's how to navigate it.
Website Costs by Type
Landing Page — €800 to €2,500
A single page built around one goal: convert visitors into leads or buyers. Good landing pages are lean, fast, and designed to do one thing well.
**Best for:** Product launches, campaign pages, lead generation funnels.
Business Website — €2,500 to €6,000
Your core online presence. Typically 5–15 pages covering services, about, contact, and blog. This is what most SMBs actually need.
**Best for:** Professional services, agencies, B2B companies, local businesses.
E-Commerce Store — €4,000 to €15,000
Online stores require product management, checkout flows, payment integrations, and order handling. Price scales with catalog size and required customizations.

items: Product catalog with search and filtering

blocks.text: **Best for:** Retailers, product brands, subscription businesses.
Custom Web Application — €7,500 to €50,000+
Web apps have business logic, user accounts, databases, real-time features, and third-party integrations. This is software, not just a website.
**Best for:** SaaS platforms, client portals, booking systems, marketplaces, internal tools.

The Hidden Ongoing Costs
The build is just the beginning. Factor in:

items: **Hosting:** Free on Vercel for Next.js; €20–€100/month for managed WordPress hosting
**Content changes:** €50–€200 per change without a CMS or retainer

blocks.text: Over 3 years, a 'cheap' €1,500 WordPress site can easily cost €5,000+ in maintenance, fixes, and hosting — more than a custom-built site with near-zero ongoing overhead.

How Much Should You Spend?
Start with what a new client is worth to you.

If one new client generates €5,000 in revenue, a website that costs €4,000 and converts even one extra lead per year pays for itself in year one. The math only works against you when the website is purely a cost center — not a revenue tool.
